jobs.name: Scout
jobs.jobLine: I watch the harbour and check every boat that brings messages into town.

introLines: Pax! Check who really sent each boat: From, Reply-To, sender check, link.
Dock the real ones, quarantine the fakes.
days.successLine: The bank boat came from bank-supp0rt with a zero, and its sender check failed. Quarantined!
days.snatchLine: That link went straight to a fake login page…
days.backupLine: I'll take the lookout. Read every sender!
days.waitingLine: Finally! The boats piled up while you were at the gate!
days.complaintLine: Hey, that was a real message!
days.complaintFailLine: Too many real boats sent away. Nobody trusts the harbour now.

fieldCard.text: A message that pretends to be someone you trust. Check the sender, the Reply-To and where the link really goes.

jobs.name: Gigi
jobs.jobLine: I keep the list of who may come in, and which door they use.

introLines: The board says: 443 Everyone, 8080 Friends only, 23 Closed.
Friend or not, a closed door stays closed.
days.successLine: Luca asked for door 23, but Telnet stays shut, even for a friend.
days.snatchLine: Door 23 was open for a moment, and a Ram walked straight in…
days.backupLine: I'll keep the gate. Show me the board!
days.waitingLine: There you are! The queue went all the way to the bridge.
days.complaintLine: That was a friend at an open door!
days.complaintFailLine: Friends kept getting turned away, so the gate stopped checking.

fieldCard.text: Each service has a door number, its port. Open only the doors you need, for the people on the list.

jobs.name: Uno and Due
jobs.jobLine: Uno checks the password. Due checks with the owner's phone. You need both of us.

introLines: Uno: A right password isn't enough on its own.
Due: The code must match, be fresh, and the owner must have asked.
days.successLine: Four approval requests in a minute? That's push bombing. We kept it shut and reported it!
days.snatchLine: Uno: The password was right… Due: but the owner never asked to log in!
days.backupLine: I'll stand by the vault. Two checks, every time.
days.waitingLine: Uno: Finally! Due: The requests kept coming!
days.complaintLine: Uno: That was really Sofia. Due: New phone, right code, and she asked.
days.complaintFailLine: Owners got locked out so often they stopped using the vault.

fieldCard.text: Attackers spam approval requests and hope you tap Yes. If you didn't ask to log in, deny it and report it.

jobs.name: Patch
jobs.jobLine: When the builders send new parts, I fit them before the old cracks get bigger.

days.alertLine: Crates incoming, and Worms on the wall!
introLines: Check the signature and who really sent it.
Real fixes go in now, before the Worms reach a crack.
days.successLine: bu1lders with a one and a bad signature? That update was fake. The real ones went in fast!
days.snatchLine: A fake update opened a crack, and the Worm got in…
days.backupLine: I'll fix the wall. Signed parts only!
days.waitingLine: There you are! The Worms are halfway up the wall!
days.complaintLine: That was a real, signed crate from the builders!
days.complaintFailLine: Too many real fixes left outside, and the wall fell apart.

fieldCard.text: An update is safe only if its signature checks out and it comes from the real maker. Fit real fixes fast.

intro: Every message you send passes through a tiny town inside your network: Byte World.
The Bytes live here. They carry your photos, chats and logins from door to door.
Lately, strangers keep sneaking in: fake messages, look-alike visitors, worms at the walls.
So the Bytes called for help, and a visitor arrived with an empty Cisco toolkit. That's you, Pax.
Gigi: A visitor! Perfect timing, Pax. Two stations need help. Follow the red rings!

dayEnd.speaker: gigi
dayEnd.title: Quest 1 done
dayEnd.line: The outer perimeter holds. Next: the inner ring.

dayEnd.speaker: patch
dayEnd.title: Quest 2 done
dayEnd.line: We found the scanner. Now we rebuild, and this time in lanes.

collapse: No Bytes were left to do the work, and the attackers took over.
peace: Built it ourselves, and built it right. Back to work, everyone!

build.speaker: patch
intro: Today we rebuild the town's network ourselves, and this time we build it right.
build.failNoPath: That house has no cable to the router. The message got lost on the way!
build.failWrongHouse: That message went to the wrong house.
build.failLeak: An attacker walked through a door we left open. Let's fix the rules!
build.success: Every message arrived where it should, and nobody sneaked in!

ui.tagline: A tiny world living inside your network

lines: Welcome to Byte World Town Space, Pax.
Phishing boats at the harbour and visitors at the gate, both at once.
Read every sender. Keep closed doors closed.
Inner ring next: the Duo Vault and Patch's Workshop.
Watch for push spam and fake updates.
Then meet me at the Splunk Observatory.
Something got in. Time to rebuild the network in lanes.
Keep the infected pod away from the vault.
The siege is here, and the Webex call keeps freezing.
If we can't see inside the cables, call the network team.

checks.question: Which detail proved the bank message was fake?
options: It had a link in it
The sender check failed and the domain used a zero
checks.explanation: Look-alike domains and a failed sender check are the classic signs of phishing.

checks.question: Why stay closed to Luca at door 23?
options: Telnet sends everything unencrypted, so it stays closed for everyone
Luca is not on the list
It was too late in the day
checks.explanation: A closed door protects the whole town. Being a friend doesn't make it safe.

checks.question: The password was correct. Why was it still an attack?
options: The owner never asked to log in, and the second factor stopped it
checks.explanation: With MFA, a stolen password alone is not enough.

checks.question: What did the Splunk search show?
options: One address scanning door 8080 again and again: reconnaissance
checks.explanation: Searching all the logs at once shows patterns no single house can see.

checks.question: Pod 12 is infected. What stops it reaching the vault?
options: The pods are on separate switch lanes
checks.explanation: Segmentation keeps an infection inside its own lane.

checks.question: What happens to traffic no rule matches?
options: It is dropped: the implicit deny
checks.explanation: A firewall allows only what a rule permits; everything else is dropped.

checks.question: How did ThousandEyes help?
options: It showed which link was losing packets, so we fixed the cause
checks.explanation: Seeing loss and latency per link turns guessing into a fix.

checks.question: Why give the Webex call priority?
options: Real-time video breaks with loss and jitter, so it goes first
checks.explanation: Quality of service lets time-sensitive traffic go first.

props.name: Rusted Door 23
props.text: Door 23 is Telnet: everything through it travels as plain text, passwords too. Modern doors encrypt.

props.name: Conduit Bridges
props.text: Each bridge is a lane. Traffic stays on its own bridge unless a rule lets it cross.

learnerCard.title: Learner Card: Byte World
outcomes: Spot phishing from the sender, Reply-To, sender check and link
Allow traffic by list and port, and keep Telnet (23) shut
Explain why a correct password isn't enough, and spot push fatigue
Reject unsigned updates and patch what matters first
Build a basic Splunk search and find a scan in the logs
Segment a network into lanes so one infection stays put
Order firewall rules for least privilege, with deny last
Find the root cause of a bad call from loss, latency and jitter
Put an incident's evidence in order, from scan to flood
